items.prompt:
Straight-down orthographic plan photograph of a built live-action film set: camera axis exactly perpendicular to the ground; no wall face, no elevation, no side of any building or tree trunk is visible; only the ground plane, the top edges of walls, the tops of roofs, furniture and tree crowns are seen. The top of the image is north. The White Rabbit's neat little two-storey red brick cottage and its yard at the edge of a wood on a hot bright July afternoon. The house footprint is a small rectangle in the centre of the image, about a quarter of the image width: blue-grey slate roof with the ridge running left to right, a few loose slipped slates near the right end, and a broad brick chimney stack with two clay pots at the right (east) gable end; a thin line of pastel-and-gold mosaic and gilded iron gutter brackets along the eaves. Along the top edge of the image runs a dry earth lane; a short swept stone path leads from the lane to the middle of the top (north) wall line, marking the front door. Below the house (south) is the kitchen-garden back yard: directly below the middle of the bottom (south) wall a low wooden cucumber-frame with sloping glass lights glinting in the sun; the lower-right corner of the yard next to the south-east corner of the house is firm level bare ground; lower left an old apple tree crown with a freshly dug patch of earth beside it; sweet peas on canes, dry sun-baked earth and summer grass; a low paling fence with flowing tops runs along the bottom of the yard with green tree crowns of the wood beyond it at the bottom edge. Climbing roses and honeysuckle along the top of the south wall. The left (west) gable and roof slope are in full sun, crisp shadows fall to the right. All walls are continuous; the bottom (south) wall is fully present, seen only as the eaves line. Door leaves, the brass plate, window sashes, fanlights and anything mounted on a wall face are not visible from directly above and must not be drawn. Clean base image for a layout plan: no people, no animals, no birds, no creatures, no text, no labels, no arrows, no grid lines, no compass.
 Photorealistic live-action fantasy film rooted in England in 1862, shot on 35mm film with anamorphic lenses, 16:9 widescreen. Real sets, real locations and real costumed actors in 1862 dress. Wonderland spaces are real built sets and set extensions in an Alphonse Mucha-inspired Art Nouveau design: flowing organic lines, floral and vine ornament, circular halo roundels, mosaic and stained glass, aged pastel-and-gold surfaces with patina and moss; the waking 1862 meadow stays plain period realism. Talking animals and fantastical creatures are photoreal CGI animals with naturalistic anatomy, real fur, feathers, skin and scales, lit by the same light and grounded with real contact shadows. Natural and practical light: sunlight, candlelight and oil lamps, soft haze with volumetric light shafts and soft colour through stained glass. Restrained palette of verdigris teal, slate grey, dusty rose, soft sage and lilac pastels and tarnished-gold accents, warmed by amber sun and candle glow. Fine film grain, gentle halation, soft depth of field, grounded and quietly melancholy.
